Mr. Sun Fo is also quoted as having expressed an opinion that there are definite, immediate prospects of the infiltration of China, and suggesting that, although the Kuominchun has been defeated, its power has not lost much. Another statement was that as Canton paid a good deal of attention to the situation along the Yangtze River (Central China), the projected Northern Expedition (from Kwangtung) would soon be a fact. The necessity of Canton's policy of expansion made it a matter of moment.
In reply to a query as to political developments, Mr. Sun Fo said that he could not make a statement till he had returned to Canton.
To an invitation to speak of the "Canton-Hongkong labour trouble," Mr. Sun Fo made no direct reply.
